info.title: Emboss
info.summary: Turn a flat PDF into a fillable form, fill it, check it, and send it.
info.description:
Emboss is a PDF form-filling API for developers and agents. Hand it a flat or scanned PDF and it detects the fields and returns a fillable form. Fill that form from structured values or from the documents that hold the answers, and Emboss proposes every answer with its source, says what is missing, and returns the finished PDF with a receipt. It also reads a filled form back into labelled values, fills one copy per spreadsheet row, packages a form with its attachments, and faxes the result. Pricing is per job in cents with a monthly free allowance.

The same engine answers on four interfaces: this REST API, a remote MCP server at /mcp, an A2A agent at /a2a, and an anonymous pay-per-call API at /pay whose own manifest is served at the origin root /openapi.json.

Documents are deleted 60 to 70 minutes after the last activity on a form under ephemeral processing.

post.summary: Price a document before you call
post.description:
Price what making a form fillable, and optionally filling it from
context documents, would cost before you actually run it.

Send the same PDF and optional context documents you would send to
POST /forms or /forms/with-context. Returns the price for each possible
next step, in cents, and whether it would be covered by your
free monthly allowance. Nothing is created, saved, or billed by this call.

post.description:
Turn a flat or scanned PDF into a fillable form.

Send the PDF as an uploaded file, or name a form already in the public
library by its slug instead (send one or the other, not both). Emboss
detects the fields and names them from the words printed beside them.
Processing runs in the background: the call returns a form_id right
away with status "processing", and GET /forms/{form_id} reports when it
turns "ready" or "failed".

delete.description:
Delete a form and the documents behind it.

This is the reversal for a fill: it takes back the documents Emboss wrote and
the sources it was given. It can be called at any time while the documents
exist. Under ephemeral processing they exist for 60 to 70 minutes after the
last activity on the form, after which Emboss deletes them anyway and there is
nothing left to take back.

If the form still has work running (a fill, a batch, a with-context job),
this answers 409 instead of deleting: the files that job needs would be
pulled out from under it.

post.summary: Create and fill a form from documents
post.description:
Make a form fillable and fill it in one call, using supporting
documents instead of typed-in values.

Send the blank form (a file, or a library slug) plus one or more context
documents (an ID, a prior filing, anything with the answers in it).
Emboss detects the form's fields, reads the context documents, and fills
what it can find. Runs as a background job: poll it with
GET /forms/with-context/{job_id} for the filled PDF and a report of
what was filled, left blank, or needs confirming.

post.description:
Turn a proposal into a finished, filled PDF. A proposal is the set of
candidate values a prepare-from-context call left on a form, not yet
committed to paper.

Send corrected values and confirmed field ids as JSON only; this call
does not accept files, so attach any new documents first on the
attachments route. A commit is free unless package is true, which an
account is billed for as one package. A proposal takes up to 10 commits,
and each runs in the background, so poll GET /forms/with-context/{job_id}
for the result or fetch the finished PDF from GET /proposals/{proposal_id}/pdf.

Checkboxes take yes or no; yes ticks that box. In a Yes/No pair, say yes
to the box you want; two yeses in one pair are refused.

post.description:
Send a PDF to a fax number.

Give the destination as `to` in E.164 form (for example +15035550100).
Send the pages as uploaded PDF files, or as JSON naming exactly one of a
finished job, a form, a PDF URL or base64 bytes. The call answers 202 with
a fax job to follow on GET /fax/{job_id}. Faxing is billed per transmitted
page, and an account needs a payment method on file to send one. Send an Idempotency-Key header so a retry never sends the fax twice.

text/plain.example:
# Emboss pay-per-call (MPP)

Agents pay Emboss per operation over HTTP using the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP). No account. Send the request, get a 402 with a payment challenge, pay, resend with the credential, get a 202 with a job to poll.

get.description: The public price list beside /pay/quote; same body as GET /pricing.

post.description:
Free, stateless inspect-before-pay: page count, whether the PDF is
already fillable, and the exact price of every op for THIS PDF, computed
with the same engine function the 402 uses. No quote row, no staging.
Shares the per-IP quote throttle with the 402 path.

example.context_text: Grace Hopper, born 9 December 1906, 1 Navy Way, Arlington, VA 22202.
example.file: <the PDF form, sent as a file>

example.next: POST /pay/<op> with the same file. The 402 challenge carries this exact price.

post.description:
Run one Emboss job and pay for it on the call itself, with no account.

This is the pay-per-call API: no account. Send the PDF and whatever that
job needs, as multipart form data or as a JSON body, naming the job in the
URL: one of make-fillable, fill, fill-with-context, read or fax. With no
payment attached the call answers 402 Payment Required and quotes a price
for this specific document, payable by card or by stablecoin; the 402
already carries the job's job_id and status_url. Send the call again
carrying the payment and it answers 202 Accepted within about 10 seconds
with the job's status: ready, working (check status_url, which is free,
every few seconds until it is ready or failed) or failed. For a fax, ready
means the carrier accepted it; keep checking until result.status is
delivered, failed or expired. A failed job runs again at no charge when
the same request is resent with the same payment (with MPP, only while
its payment challenge is valid), up to three runs in all.

Every call costs money, priced per job from the document you send, so the
page count and the context you attach change the price. Nothing here is
billed to an account, because there is no account: the payment on the call
is the whole arrangement. To see a price before committing to it, POST the
document to /pay/quote, which is free and prices every job for that exact
PDF without running anything or storing it.

example.file: <the PDF form, sent as a file>

get.description:
Check on a paid job, free: the job's status in one plain word.

status is awaiting_payment (priced, not yet paid), working (still running:
check again after poll_after_seconds, also sent as Retry-After), ready
(result carries the output and, for a job that produces a file, a download
link that stays the same on every check), failed (error says why; retry,
when present, says how to run it again at no charge) or expired (the
result's files are deleted, about an hour after the job, or a price that
was never paid has expired). For a fax, ready means the carrier accepted
it; keep checking until result.status is delivered, failed or expired.
quote_status keeps the quote's own older word. The 402 and the 202 both
carry this link, token included, as status_url.

post.description:
Register a new OAuth client app with Emboss (dynamic client
registration, RFC 7591).

Send the app's name, redirect URIs, and how it authenticates. Returns a
client_id (and a client_secret, if the app authenticates with one) to
use in the authorize and token calls that follow. No prior credential
needed; this is how a new integration gets one.

get.description:
Start the sign-in and consent step of the OAuth flow.

A browser is sent here with the client's client_id, redirect_uri, and a
PKCE code challenge, per standard OAuth 2.1 authorization-code flow.
Emboss redirects on to its own consent page for the user to approve,
then back to the client's redirect_uri with an authorization code (or
an error) to exchange at POST /oauth/token.

302.description: Redirect: to sign in and consent, or back to the client's redirect_uri with code and state, or with an RFC 6749 section 4.1.2.1 error.

400.description: An unknown client or an unregistered redirect address: an error page, never a redirect.

post.description:
Exchange an authorization code, or a refresh token, for an access
token.

Send a form-encoded body with grant_type set to authorization_code
(with the code from /oauth/authorize and its PKCE verifier) or
refresh_token (with a token from a previous exchange). Returns a
bearer access_token plus a refresh_token to renew it once it expires.

Revoke an access or refresh token, ending that sign-in (RFC 7009).

Send the token as a form field, authenticated as the client that
received it. Once revoked, the whole family of tokens it belongs to
stops working; a client should call this when a user disconnects the
integration.

200.description: Revoked, or the token was already invalid; the body is empty (RFC 7009 section 2.2).

401.description: The client could not be authenticated (RFC 6749 section 5.2).
